definition_en: a structure with walls and a roof, or the act of constructing
core_image: 一栋楼从地面立起，窗子一层层往上排，像叠起的格子
scene: 街角那栋楼一层层往上排着窗子，傍晚灯一盏盏亮起。 The new building has ten floors.
sceneCN: 这里 building 是「建筑物」（第 01 个义项）；句意是这栋新楼有十层。

pos.zh: 名词：建筑物、建造、建筑业

senses.title: A structure with walls and a roof
senses.definition: a structure with walls and a roof, such as a house or an office
senses.definitionCN: 有墙有顶的建筑，如住宅或办公楼
senses.example: The new building has ten floors.
senses.why: Building is build plus -ing, and the ending can name the finished thing: what has been built.
senses.whyCN: building 是 build 加 -ing，这个词尾可以指完成的结果，也就是「建成的东西」。

senses.title: The act or process of constructing
senses.definition: the work or process of constructing something
senses.example: The building of the bridge took two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥的建造花了两年。
senses.why: The same -ing form also names the activity itself, so the building of a bridge is the work, not the finished bridge.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 -ing 形式也能指活动本身，所以 the building of a bridge 说的是施工，不是建成的桥。

senses.title: The construction industry
senses.definition: the industry that designs and puts up structures
senses.definitionCN: 设计与建造房屋的行业
senses.example: He works in building.
senses.why: Once the whole trade of putting up structures is treated as one field, building becomes the name of that industry.
senses.whyCN: 当建造房屋这一整行当被看成一个领域，building 就成了这个行业的名称。

definition_en: the dark shape cast by an object blocking light, or a hidden darkness, or to follow someone secretly
core_image: 午后阳光斜照，孩子踩着自己的影子走过操场，树影在地上拉得很长
scene: 午后阳光斜照，孩子踩着自己的影子走过操场，树影在地上拉得很长。 The tree casts a long shadow.
sceneCN: 这里 shadow 是「影子」（第 01 个义项）；句意是树投下长长的影子。

senses.title: The dark shape cast by an object
senses.definition: The dark shape cast by an object
senses.definitionCN: 物体挡住光留下的暗形
senses.example: The tree casts a long shadow.
senses.why: Old English sceadu named shade; a shadow is the shape that shade takes on the ground.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 sceadu 指荫蔽，shadow 则是荫蔽在地面上显出的形状。

senses.title: A darkness or a bad feeling left behind
senses.definition: A darkness or a bad feeling left behind
senses.definitionCN: 留下的暗处或心头的阴霾
senses.example: A shadow of doubt crossed her face.
senses.exampleCN: 她脸上掠过一丝疑虑的阴影。
senses.why: Because a shadow darkens what it falls on, the word also names gloom in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 因为影子会让所落之处变暗，这个词也指心头的阴郁。

senses.title: To follow someone secretly
senses.definition: To follow someone secretly
senses.example: A stranger shadowed him to the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 一个陌生人悄悄跟着他到了门口。
senses.why: To shadow a person is to stay in their shadow, unseen, so the noun became a verb for secret following.
senses.whyCN: shadow 一个人就是待在他的影子里不被看见，名词由此转为暗中跟踪的动词。

definition_en: what people or animals eat, a kind of dish, or material that feeds plants
core_image: 餐桌上摆着一碗热汤、一盘米饭和一碟青菜
scene: 餐桌上摆着一碗热汤、一盘米饭和一碟青菜。 There is enough food for everyone.
sceneCN: 这里 food 是「食物」（第 01 个义项）；句意是食物够所有人吃。

senses.title: What people eat
senses.definition: what people or animals eat
senses.example: There is enough food for everyone.
senses.why: Old English foda meant nourishment; the word names whatever is eaten to keep a body alive.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 foda 意为「养料」；这个词指为维持生命而吃下的一切。

senses.title: A cuisine or dish
senses.definition: a particular kind or dish of food
senses.example: I love Chinese food.
senses.why: The same mass noun is used for a cuisine or a dish, naming food by its style rather than by its substance.
senses.whyCN: 同一个不可数名词也用来指某种菜系或菜式，按风格而不是按物质来指食物。

senses.title: Material that feeds plants
senses.definition: material that feeds plants
senses.example: Plant food helps the roses grow.
senses.exampleCN: 花肥能让玫瑰长得更好。
senses.why: Because the word means nourishment in general, it also names what is fed to plants, as in plant food.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词泛指养分，它也指喂给植物的东西，如 plant food。

senses.definitionCN: 离地面远、从底到顶距离大
senses.example: The wall is two meters high.

senses.whyCN: 古英语 heah 意为高耸；这个词属日耳曼语，本指空间上的高度。

senses.whyCN: 因为高度可以用刻度衡量，high 就从物理空间延伸到价格、分数与标准。

senses.title: Sharp in pitch
senses.definition: Sharp in pitch
senses.example: She sang a high note.

senses.whyCN: 音调升高让人感觉向上，所以 high 也形容尖而高的音符。

definition_en: a tool with prongs, to divide into branches, or to lift with a fork
core_image: 餐盘旁边摆着一把银色餐叉，叉齿朝上
scene: 餐盘旁边摆着一把银色餐叉，叉齿朝上。 He ate the cake with a fork.
sceneCN: 这里 fork 是「叉子」（第 01 个义项）；句意是他用叉子吃蛋糕。

senses.title: A pronged tool
senses.definition: a tool with prongs for eating or lifting
senses.definitionCN: 带齿的进食或取物工具
senses.example: He ate the cake with a fork.
senses.why: Fork comes from Latin furca, a two-pronged pitchfork; the table tool kept the shape and the name.
senses.whyCN: fork 源自拉丁语 furca，即两齿的干草叉；餐具保留了它的形状和名字。

senses.title: To split in two
senses.definition: to divide into two branches
senses.example: The road forks after the bridge.
senses.why: The shape of a two-pronged fork gave the verb its sense: a path that splits looks like the two prongs.
senses.whyCN: 两齿叉的形状给出了动词义：分开的路就像叉子的两个齿。

senses.title: To lift with a fork
senses.definition: to lift or move with a fork
senses.example: She forked the meat onto the plate.
senses.exampleCN: 她用叉子把肉叉到盘子里。
senses.why: English made a verb from the noun, so to fork is to use the tool that bears its name.
senses.whyCN: 英语由名词造出动词，to fork 就是使用名为 fork 的工具。

senses.title: A stick of coloured wax for drawing
senses.definition: a small stick of coloured wax or chalk used for drawing
senses.definitionCN: 画画用的彩色蜡或粉制小棒
senses.example: The child draws a sun with a red crayon.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子用红蜡笔画了个太阳。

senses.example: That crayon on the wall is her best work.
senses.exampleCN: 墙上那幅蜡笔画是她最好的作品。
senses.why: The name of a drawing tool often passes to the picture made with it, and crayon followed that path from stick to drawing.
senses.whyCN: 画具的名字常常转指用它画成的作品，crayon 也从画笔延伸到了画本身。

definition_en: to move from one place to another, to become, or to proceed
core_image: 一个人背起包，沿着路向前走，身后的门刚刚关上
scene: 清晨他背起包出门，沿着路一直向前走。 We go to school by bus every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 go 是「去」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我们每天早上坐公交车去学校。

senses.title: To move or travel to a place
senses.definition: to move from one place to another, especially away from the speaker
senses.definitionCN: 从一个地方移动到另一个地方，尤指离开说话人所在处
senses.example: We go to school by bus every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 我们每天早上坐公交车去学校。
senses.why: Go goes back to Old English gān, 'to walk, to leave a place', and movement away is still its centre.
senses.whyCN: go 来自古英语 gān「行走、离开某处」，离开原地仍是它的核心。

senses.title: To become a particular state
senses.definition: to change into a stated condition, usually a bad one
senses.definitionCN: 转入某种状态，通常是不好的状态
senses.example: The milk went bad in the heat.
senses.why: A thing that 'goes' from one condition to another has travelled there, so go plus an adjective means 'become'.
senses.whyCN: 事物从一个状态「走」到另一个状态，就像到了别处，所以 go 加形容词表示「变得」。

senses.title: To work or run
senses.definition: to operate or function, said of a machine
senses.example: The old clock still goes.
senses.why: A machine that runs is one that keeps moving, so the movement verb also describes working order.
senses.whyCN: 机器能运转就是能一直动，所以这个表示移动的词也描述工作状态。

senses.title: An attempt or a turn
senses.definition: an attempt to do something, or a turn in a game
senses.definitionCN: 试着做一次，或在游戏里轮一回
senses.example: Let me have a go at the puzzle.
senses.why: The noun go comes from the idea of one trip or one turn at something, as in have a go.
senses.whyCN: 名词 go 来自「走一趟、来一回」的说法，如 have a go。

senses.title: The sweet food made from cacao
senses.definition: a sweet brown food made from cacao beans
senses.definitionCN: 用可可豆做成的棕色甜食
senses.example: She breaks the chocolate into squares.
senses.why: Chocolate came into English through Spanish, from a Nahuatl word for a bitter cacao drink, and it now names the sweet food made from cacao.
senses.whyCN: chocolate 经西班牙语进入英语，源自阿兹特克语里一种苦味可可饮料的名字，现在指可可做成的甜食。

senses.title: One small sweet of this kind
senses.definition: a single small sweet made of chocolate
senses.definitionCN: 一颗用巧克力做的小糖
senses.example: He gave her a box of chocolates.
senses.exampleCN: 他送给她一盒巧克力糖。
senses.why: A single piece can be counted, so a chocolate is one sweet and chocolates are the pieces in a box.
senses.whyCN: 单块的巧克力可以数，所以 a chocolate 就是一颗糖，chocolates 就是一盒里的那些块。

senses.title: A hot drink made with chocolate
senses.definition: a hot drink made by melting chocolate in milk or water
senses.definitionCN: 把巧克力化在牛奶或水里做成的热饮
senses.example: A cup of hot chocolate warms the hands.
senses.why: Melted chocolate mixed with milk becomes a drink, and the same word covers that hot drink.
senses.whyCN: 化开的巧克力兑上牛奶就成了饮料，同一个词也指这种热饮。

definition_en: causing laughter, strange, or slightly unwell
core_image: 同学讲了一个笑话，全班笑得趴在桌上
scene: 同学讲了一个笑话，全班笑得趴在桌上。 She told a funny story.
sceneCN: 这里 funny 是「好笑的」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她讲了一个好笑的故事。

senses.title: Causing laughter
senses.definition: causing laughter
senses.example: She told a funny story.
senses.exampleCN: 她讲了一个好笑的故事。
senses.why: Funny is fun plus -y; fun first meant a joke or a diversion, so funny describes what produces that kind of amusement.
senses.whyCN: funny 是 fun 加 -y；fun 最初指玩笑或消遣，funny 就形容能产生这种乐趣的东西。

senses.title: Strange or hard to explain
senses.definition: strange or hard to explain
senses.example: There is a funny smell in the kitchen.
senses.why: Because something amusing can also be odd, the same word slid into 'strange', especially when a thing feels slightly wrong.
senses.whyCN: 因为引人发笑的东西也可能古怪，这个词又滑向「奇怪」，尤其当某物让人觉得不太对劲时。

senses.title: Slightly unwell
senses.definition: slightly unwell
senses.example: I feel funny after that ride.
senses.exampleCN: 坐完那趟车我有点不舒服。
senses.why: The 'odd' sense applies to how the body feels, so feel funny means feeling slightly ill or dizzy.

senses.title: To go up using the hands and feet

senses.example: They climb the hill before sunrise.

senses.example: Prices climbed all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 整个夏天价格都在上涨。

senses.whyCN: 上升的数字像攀登者一样往上走，所以这个攀爬的动词也描述持续增长。

senses.exampleCN: 爬到山顶是一段很长的攀登。
